chapters.source_excerpt: ## Introducing Ali (ع) and his Spiritual Ethos I am the city of knowledge and Ali (ع) is its gate; so whoever desires knowledge, let him enter the gate. chapters.title: The People of the House and the Prophet's Witness
source_headings: The Prophet said that Ali (ع) was 'as my own soul' (ka-nafsi).
He said to Ali (ع), 'You are from me and I am from you (anta minnī wa anā minka), أنْتَ مِنِّی وَ أِنَا مِنْکَ.'
chapters.source_excerpt: Ali (ع)'s role as a warrior is only one of many factors that account for his unique place in the Islamic tradition. Far more significant is his closeness, in every respect, to the Prophet and the wisdom and sanctity that flowed from that proximity. chapters.title: Justice for the Poor and the Sincerity of Intention
chapters.source_excerpt: The Imam now turns to a point in the letter he wants Malik to take especially to heart: the poor, those most in need of justice. He opens the passage with the exclamation 'Allah, Allah' to signal its urgency. chapters.title: Extinction and the Name: The Death of the Saint
source_headings: He said, 'I am wielding the sword for God's sake, I am the servant of God, I am not under the command of the body.
I have removed the baggage of self out of the way, I have deemed (what is) other than God to be non-existence.
I am a shadow, the Sun is my lord; I am the chamberlain, I am not the curtain (which prevents approach) to Him.
chapters.source_excerpt: The first point to be made by way of response is this: the individual cannot on his own make this leap from remembrance to forgetfulness. It is impossible for a conscious person, concentrating on the invocatory act, to render himself unconscious of himself in the course of that invocation.
